# Fortress revival

This is @palimondo's revival of Sun/Oracle's **Fortress** programming language
(Guy Steele's HPC language, 2003–2012; interpreter + partial JVM compiler,
BSD-licensed). The repo is a 2018 GitHub fork of `sirinath/fortress`, a git
conversion of the project's java.net Mercurial repository: 5,397 trunk commits
from 2007-01-04 to 2012-08-31 (`a874948ac`), twelve old branches and the `1.0`
tag. The conversion cut 146 parent links, so a history walk from HEAD stops
early; see `research/authorship.md`. Everything after `a874948ac` is the
revival's own work (2026). Working mode: Claude explains the
codebase and produces documentation and experiments as we go; Pavol decides
what gets committed. The full collaboration protocol — roles, tone, how work
is presented, commit discipline, delegation — is in
`explorations/protocol.md`; read it at session start.
The coordinator's knowledge base — `explorations/coordinator/` (`FACTS.md`: what is
established, with sources; `POSITIONS.md`: what Pavol has decided and already knows) — is
read at session start and after every compaction, and updated in the same commit as the
work that establishes a fact or takes a decision; the current state of the work is in
`explorations/microgpt-run-c-handover.md`.

## Build and run

```bash
apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant  # JDK 8, 11, 17 and 21 also build and gate green
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
export FORTRESS_HOME=<repo root>
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS                          # proxy trust-store options confuse ant's JVM forks
cd $FORTRESS_HOME && ant compileAll              # ~80 s
./bin/fortress explorations/claude_demo.fss      # interpreter ("walk")
```

Toolchain traps: `build.xml` drives scalac through `scala.tools.nsc.Main`
directly, because Scala 2.13 dropped the `scala.tools.ant` tasks; ASM is
vendored in `ProjectFortress/third_party/asm/`, and Fortress's own
`asmbytecodeoptimizer.Opcodes` shadows `org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes` in that
package; sources are compiled as UTF-8. The versions, the emitted classfile
level and the runtime's ForkJoin pool are in
`explorations/modernization-plan.md`.

Facts that save time:

- **Both execution paths work.** `fortress <file>.fss` interprets directly.
  The bytecode compiler path (`fortress compile` + `fortress run`) has two
  traps: imported library components (`System`, `CompilerSystem`) must be
  explicitly `fortress compile`d into the cache first, and **stale caches**
  cause a misleading `NoSuchMethodError: fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println(...)`
  — wipe `default_repository/caches/*` and recompile in library order (recipe
  in `explorations/repo-internals.md`). The compiler is incomplete (some
  constructs still `sayWhat`), not broken.
- **`ProjectFortress/hello.fss` runs only via the compiler path** — its July
  2012 upgrade imports `System.getProperty`/`CompilerSystem.args`, which the
  interpreter can't resolve. Use `explorations/*.fss` as interpreter smoke
  tests.
- **The test suite is fully green and is the gate for every change:** `ant
  testFast` (the compiler suite among others) and `ant testSystem` (the
  interpreter tests), zero failures. The current counts are in the last
  landed gate summary (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt`);
  how the suite first went green is in `explorations/test-baseline-jdk8.md`.
- The interpreter requires filename (sans `.fss`) == component name.
- If scalac fails with arity errors in `S*Pattern` nodes, the generated AST
  sources are stale relative to `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`:
  `touch ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast && ant compileAll` regenerates.
- Interpreter caches live in `default_repository/caches/` (gitignored); wipe
  them if library edits seem to have no effect.
- Architecture map, name-resolution rules, cache anatomy, test-harness
  mechanics, and git-archaeology techniques: `explorations/repo-internals.md`
  — read it before diving into the source.

## Layout

- Original Fortress tree: everything not listed below — do not modify
  casually; it is the historical artifact being revived.
- `explorations/` — revival-era experiments and writeups (ours; verified
  running programs).
- `research/` — the Guy Steele corpus: `research/README.md` is a committed
  links-only index; `research/extracts/` holds committed working notes;
  `research/decks/` is **gitignored** (copyrighted PDFs, dropped in per
  session, never committed).
- `Specification/` + `Specification-1.0-frozen/` — the language spec LaTeX
  (in-repo, richer than the published PDF; building it is untested).

## Project goal

Finish what the designers intended, judged by the specification in
`Specification/`, the Working Draft of 2010-12 as the revival revises it, not
redesign the language; the measuring stick is one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode
and running fast (Pavol, 2026-09-16, `explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md`).
`Specification/` stays the standard; where the Types chapter of the team's
later, unfinished restart of the specification
(`Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, 2012) covers a
topic, it is cited beside it as the designers' later word (Pavol, 2026-09-26;
`explorations/coordinator/spec-lineage.md`).
The plan is `explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`; where the work stands is the
first section of `explorations/microgpt-run-c-handover.md`; every known gap,
defect and design limit is a row of `explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md`.

Claims in the 2012 tree's own READMEs (root `README.txt` among them) describe
their era, not the current tree — verify against the code before acting on
them.

- The code generator lowers every type to a JVM reference type: `RR64` to the runtime class `FRR64`, no `dadd`/`dmul` anywhere in the generated loop (shown in bytecode, `perf-probes/boxing/javap/`); arrays are library objects over `get`/`put`, not `double[]` (`repo-internals.md:129`).

On the interpreter, the only path that runs the kernels, 43.5% is the AST walk, 32.3% environment lookup, 5.2% type dispatch and 0% number representation (JFR on `krows`). The two one-line runtime defects the probe found are fixed (rows 302, 303; the next two entries), and no array type goes into the compiler prelude: the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (POSITIONS, the library route). A failed compile leaves a 0-byte jar in the bytecode cache (`perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md`).
- The boxing probe's scalar-loop reading, 156× primitive Java with boxing about 2% of it, is of the tree before rung 0's two fixes (rows 302, 303; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`); of the costs it named, `countedseqloop`'s boxed indices and closure call (about 7%) and the representational rest (about 30%) are unaddressed (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- The eager debug string of `BaseTask.inATransaction()` is fixed: the message is built only under the `debug` flag (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:248`; row 302; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `FFloatLiteral`'s String round trip is fixed: the literal caches its `double` instead of re-parsing its text in `asRR64()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FFloatLiteral.java`; row 303; `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- The benchmark numbers on record from 2026-09-15 (`bench1t` 9.3441 s, `bench1h` 6.0732 s) were taken on a quieter machine: the same unmodified tree measured 13.0566 s and 8.8159 s in another session, so absolute seconds are not comparable across sessions and only a before/after pair taken in one session is (`compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`).
- `ant compileAll` leaves the bytecode cache holding no library jars: the first `fortress compile` after a rebuild of the compiler clears `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/`, and `fortress run` then dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`; the library-order recompile of `repo-internals.md:170-179` restores it, about two minutes.
- The compiled path's bytecode cache can come up empty after a library-order rebuild that reports exit 0; re-running the same commands one at a time produced the jars (`perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md`).
- Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode (`InstantiatingClassloader.java`, `repo-internals.md:129`); a size is in the stamped class's name (`pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, `perf-probes/nat/java.md` § 1; `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md`), and its descriptor in a stamped class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics).
- Implicit parallelism: `for` is parallel unless every generator is `seq`; the elements of a tuple and the operands of an operator are evaluated in parallel implicit threads (`tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`; row 265). `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool; there is no explicit threading in any of our programs.
- The compile path's checker cannot check `nat` parameters at all (see "The checker and the one library" below): this no longer holds. The checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters ("The compiled type checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters" below), and a sized program loads and runs compiled ("A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`" under Landed semantics). Sizes in types (`nat` parameters) are "instantiated at runtime" by the specification (`trait-parameters.tex`, natparams); they check shapes when a value is made or passed; no optimization is built on them anywhere. A `nat`-typed parameter does not unify statically with a run-time-built array (row 23); the interpreter matches at dispatch, and a mismatch reads "Failed to find any matching overload", uncatchable (row 83). A literal size does unify (row 23's positive half).
- **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** The Working Draft's `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`, kept in `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:61-65` marked "Not allowed") stops on both paths with a syntax error at `excludes`, because the grammar gives an object no `excludes` clause (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:84-86`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothing.fss` and its captures). Without that clause, `fortress compile` and `fortress walk` give the identical single error, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`; `reviews/spec-refused-examples/probes/SpecNothingNoExcludes.fss`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4093`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind the library's comment on its parametric `Nothing[\T\]`, "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working" (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1449-1450`), and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's** (`compile-ladder/rung-export-var/`). Both paths assume an api and its implementing component share a name: `fortress link` and `walk` print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path", and the compiled run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError`. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`linker/Linker.java:72-76`); only `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` register another. The specification resolves an imported api to a component that exports it (`Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35`), and the team reserved the codegen half in `CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`. Gated as an expected failure by `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it** (`compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` and `SpanAbsorb.txt`; ledger row 359). `createSpan` (`parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) trims back over space characters only; a declaration ending in `end` is unaffected. - **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees** (`compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md`, section 4.1): `throw new FortressError((FObject) Driver.getFortressLibrary().getRootValue(name))` from a `builtinPrimitive` method reaches `Evaluator.forTry` unchanged; the helper is `Int.overflow()` (`interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:258-261`). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. The natives that raise `IntegerOverflow` so are those of "The interpreter's integer rules" and "Under `walk`, fixed-width integer arithmetic raises `IntegerOverflow` when the result does not fit" under Landed semantics, with the narrowing checks `Int.rc` and `NN32.rc` (row 347 closed). A chosen generic instance that converts an argument dispatches again (`convertedCall`, `:1307-1324`), not for overloaded methods. The symbolic instantiation is keyed by each static parameter's kind and bounds (`GenericFunctionOrMethod.java:57-68`; row 478, fixed), not by a `where` clause (`FGenericFunction.java:49-51`). Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss`, `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss` and `GenericOverloadBoundsApart.fss`.

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
